parallel.requirements: Recognized the reverse-engineering task, srgn 0.14.1 identity, behavioral-observation-only rules, offline dependency constraint, CLI/help/action/language-scope breadth, and no source lookup or wrapping requirement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and launched a sixteen-child workflow for broad behavioral exploration; children owned probe notes by area while the parent concurrently wrote the Rust project.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a dependency-free Rust regex subsystem, Unicode tables, help assets, and a temporary main smoke test, but did not complete the full srgn CLI, action pipeline, file discovery, language scoping, or packaging script.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote source in /workspace and copied help assets, but the workflow aggregate never returned; artifact validation was false and the final response file is empty after timeout.
parallel.verification: Verification was limited to local cargo build of the regex-focused smoke binary and behavior probes against the reference executable; no integrated evaluator-aligned srgn acceptance run occurred before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final parallel artifact contained only a partial implementation, lacked a complete deliverable pipeline, and official evaluation completed as compile_failed with 0/2080 quality despite extensive child probing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same cleanroom srgn reimplementation constraints, the offline Rust-only dependency situation, and the need to infer behavior from README and CLI execution.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used one local trajectory with no delegation; the same actor probed behavior, planned the Rust project, wrote compile.sh, and began implementing the regex foundation.
serial.implementation: Performed many targeted behavioral probes for CLI output, scopes, actions, Unicode, German and symbols behavior, then wrote Rust regex AST, parser, executor, and module files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created a Cargo skeleton with compile.sh that would copy target/release/srgn to ./executable, so artifact packaging itself was accepted, but the codebase remained incomplete.
serial.verification: Serial checked many reference behaviors but did not reach an integrated build or end-to-end srgn verification after writing the partial regex implementation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out and official evaluation completed as compile_failed with 0/2080 quality; the main CLI and language/action modules were absent or incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the cleanroom reimplementation rules and breadth of srgn behavior, including no source lookup, no wrapping, and behavioral probing only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the identical task constraints and probed the same srgn CLI and documentation under the cleanroom rules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference; both understood the task, but neither completed the full behavioral surface before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split exploration into sixteen workflow children while the parent independently owned the implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, and packaging in one actor with workflows disabled and no subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained broad concurrent probes but introduced a large workflow lifecycle; serial had simpler ownership and no child coordination surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children were briefed to write detailed scratch notes and concise summaries, but the aggregate workflow result stayed null and the parent saw only partial scratch outputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried observations directly in the same context and moved from probes into implementation without cross-agent handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context boundary was at workflow return and scratch-note transfer; serial avoided that boundary but had less breadth.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo project focused on regex, Unicode classes, help assets, and a smoke-test main.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Cargo skeleton with compile.sh and regex modules, then continued help-format extraction rather than completing the tool.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced more generated assets and a built smoke binary, while serial produced a cleaner compile-script skeleton; both remained far short of a full srgn clone.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow children did not converge into a returned result; state shows killed status and result null after repeated stalls and retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because delegation tools were disabled and protocol validation saw no parallel work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the intended child-result lifecycle entirely, while serial had no join or retrieval step to manage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote shared scratch probe directories and some notes while the parent wrote final source files in /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly in /workspace and used temporary probe files without concurrent child writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared scratch-state provenance to interpret, but there is no proven final source collision; serial state was simpler and artifact packaging was accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed a cargo build and smoke execution only for the regex-focused temporary binary, then official evaluation failed at compile stage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial gathered behavioral examples but did not perform an integrated build after writing partial modules; official evaluation also failed at compile stage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a local compile of a partial smoke binary, whereas serial had no comparable final build evidence; neither closed evaluator-aligned acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a workflow with 32 child logs, 1.88M workflow-child tokens, repeated stalled retries, and exited via timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with 0 subagents, no delegation, and lower total token use; artifact packaging passed despite compile failure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantial budget on a killed fan-out with no aggregate result; serial spent the window locally and avoided workflow overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status records make this a both_fail pair: both completed ProgramBench evaluation with compile_failed and 0/2080 quality. Parallel differed by launching a 16-child exploration workflow and writing a regex-focused Rust project while the workflow was killed without an aggregate result; serial stayed single-agent, built a compile.sh skeleton, and also stopped with only partial regex code. The concrete task-solving difference is process and artifact shape, not a pass/fail divergence.
parallel_contributors: Sixteen broad workflow probes with repeated stalls consumed child-token and wall-clock budget without returning a final aggregate result.
The parent implemented only a regex-focused subset and local smoke binary before timeout; artifact validation was false.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all probing and implementation local, created compile.sh, and artifact validation was true.
Serial still timed out before completing CLI, action, language, and integration code, so official evaluation compile_failed too.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts underestimated the breadth of srgn and left the main executable incomplete.
Parallel produced more generated Unicode/help assets but no full implementation; serial produced a compile script but only partial regex modules.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause; no discordant official outcome exists in current status.json evaluations

The parallel parent launched one workflow that fanned out sixteen exhaustive behavioral probes. The workflow state shows repeated stall retries, status killed, and result null, while the official run ended at timeout. That left the parent with no aggregate child findings and only a partial regex-focused implementation, whereas the serial control spent its budget in one local trajectory and at least assembled a compile.sh-based submission. Because both official evaluations failed, this is a realized parallel process cost rather than an outcome-differential root cause.
candidates.realized_consequence: The exploratory workflow consumed time and child-token budget, was killed with no aggregate result, and the parent closed at timeout with only a partial implementation and failed artifact/evaluation status.
candidates.near_match_reason: Child interruptions are visible, but the directly corrective boundary is reducing or staging the excessive fan-out rather than labeling each terminal child cancellation.
